predecessors.note: Dantidurga took the north in 753; Krishna I defeated Kirtivarman II, the last Badami Chalukya emperor, in 757 (Cliopatria's Chalukya row ends 756).

land.text: the Rashtrakuta core, taken by Tailapa II when he 'dethroned Karka' in 973

successors.note: Cliopatria starts the Western Chalukya row only in 980; the page dates Tailapa's seizure to 973. The Ganga-backed remnant under Indra IV (973-982) lay in Gangavadi and goes to western-ganga-dynasty (second successor).

land.text: Indra IV's remnant in Ganga country

successors.note: The 982 remnant lies wholly in Gangavadi, which the Gangas held as Rashtrakuta feudatories (819-982) and then until the Chola conquest; the Western Chalukyas took the core in 973 (Tailapa II page).

capitals.name: Achalapura (Elichpur)
capitals.note: The page says Dantidurga 'probably ruled from Achalapura' and that Elichpur 'remained the capital until Amoghavarsha I built Manyakheta'; Mayurkhandi (Morkhandi) is named as an early capital candidate and Govinda III's 800 campaign set out from it. The Dhruva and Krishna I pages place their deaths (793, 774) at Manyakheta, which sits oddly with a later foundation.

capitals.name: Manyakheta (Malkhed)
capitals.note: Amoghavarsha I (reign from 814) 'made Manyakheta his capital', which 'remained the Rashtrakutas' regal capital until the end of the empire'; the page does not date the move. Siyaka sacked it in 972 and the Western Chalukyas annexed it (Tailapa II page).

rulers.name: Amoghavarsha I
rulers.note: Another source cited on his page gives 815-877.

rulers.name: Indra IV
rulers.note: After 973 a claimant, supported by the Ganga chief Marasimha (Tailapa II page); died by sallekhana at Shravanabelagola, 20 March 982.

757: Krishna I takes Gangavadi from the Western Gangas. The page says he 'defeated Sripurusha and acquired territory in Gangavadi' without a year inside 756-774; 757 is the year Cliopatria's shape reaches the Mysore plateau. 790: Dhruva returns to the South. 'returned to the South in 790'.
790: the Doab is left. 'returned to the South in 790'.

region.text: Gangavadi, where 'a Ganga resurgence gained them partial control'

ledger.note: 819: Gangavadi leaves the direct land. 'by 819, a Ganga resurgence gained them partial control over Gangavadi under King Rachamalla' (Western Ganga page); the year is the page's, the land is the Mysore plateau of Cliopatria's shape (confidence 2). Mirror of western-ganga-dynasty /ledger/9 (occupation_end) and /ledger/10 (vassal_start), both 819. The Ganga page also says the Gangas 'offered stiff resistance for about a century' after 753.

819 (bridge): the Gangas are Rashtrakuta feudatories from the peace of Amoghavarsha I. 'their loyal feudatory, the Western Ganga Dynasty', 'the vassal Ganga king Shivamara II', 'the feudatory Western Ganga King Butuga II' (Dynasty page, none dated); 'the Gangas were feudatories and close allies' and finally 'accepted Rashtrakuta overlordship' (Western Ganga page). Drawn as a vassal tint, as western-ganga-dynasty /ledger/10 does; the earlier version of this dossier drew Gangavadi as direct land to 972.
821: the revolts ended. 'Re-established by 821' with the help of his cousin Karka (Surat records and Baroda plates of 835).

850: Kalinga (Odisha) drops out of Cliopatria's shape. No page opened says who took it; the Bhauma-Kara page shows a kingdom 'in a bad shape' in c. 846 (Dhenkanal inscription of Tribhuvana-Mahadevi I) and ruling Toshala again after the Rashtrakuta-Pala domination, so the Bhauma-Karas are named, confidence 1.
850: Kosala (Chhattisgarh) drops out of Cliopatria's shape; no page opened says who took it, so nobody.

region.text: Srisailam and the Andhra and Telangana interior

ledger.note: 850: the Srisailam country drops out of Cliopatria's shape (33,636 km2); no page opened says who took it.

region.text: Vengi: the 150 km disc around Vijayawada without the land Cliopatria's 850 shape keeps

ledger.note: 850: the Eastern Chalukya feudatory is gone from the Rashtrakuta shape; the page does not say how the relation ended.

region.text: Gujarat: Cliopatria's 850 shape without its 860 shape

ledger.note: 860: Gujarat leaves the Rashtrakuta shape for the Pratiharas (107,988 km2, 105,459 of it in Gujarat, 99.8 percent inside Cliopatria's Gurjara-Pratihara 860 shape). 'Bhoja was able to retain dominion over parts of Gujarat and Malwa' and 'by the end of his reign, Bhoja had successfully exterminated the Gujarat Rashtrakuta line' (Gurjara-Pratihara page, both undated). 860 is Cliopatria's year and that of gurjara-pratihara-dynasty /ledger/20, whose mirror this is; confidence 1.

860 (moved from 888): the Gujarat branch tint ends where the Pratihara shape takes the land. The Dynasty page: 'Well known among these were the Rashtrakutas of Gujarat (757-888)' and 'Krishna II ended the independent status of the Gujarat branch and brought it under direct control from Manyakheta'; the Gurjara-Pratihara page: 'Around 880, the Gurjara-Pratiharas were defeated in large battle in Ujjain by Krishna II, the Rastrakuta king of Gujarat' and Bhoja 'had successfully exterminated the Gujarat Rashtrakuta line'. The pages disagree with each other and with Cliopatria, which gives Gujarat to the Pratiharas from 860 (the Pratihara dossier draws it so), so no 888 gain of Gujarat is drawn and the tint cannot run on over Pratihara land: 888 stays in this note only.

916: Indra III takes Kannauj. The page says the Rashtrakutas held Kannauj 'until c. 916'; the Gurjara-Pratihara page: 'in about 916 sacked Kannauj'. The year of the entry is the sack's; Mahipala I fled.

926: Kannauj is back in Pratihara hands. The Indra III page has the Rashtrakutas hold Kannauj 'until c. 916'; the Gurjara-Pratihara page says only 'although the Pratiharas regained the city' (no year). 926 is the year of gurjara-pratihara-dynasty /ledger/24 (Cliopatria restores Kannauj in 926), to which this end is aligned (an earlier version stood at 917, a bridge); the contest zone therefore stays blended 916-926, confidence 1.

944: Krishna III secures Tondaimandalam from the Cholas. 'Tondaimandalam was secured by 944'; the Siddalingamadam plates of 944 record the capture of Kanchi and Tanjore. Cliopatria keeps Kanchi in the Chola shape through 975.
944: war with the Cholas over Kanchi and Tanjore (Siddalingamadam plates of 944).
949: Takkolam. 'In c. 949, he defeated the Cholas decisively in a Battle of Takkolam'; the page does not tie the earlier gains to this battle.
967: Tondaimandalam is not Rashtrakuta after Krishna III. No page opened dates its loss; Krishna III's reign ends December 967 and Cliopatria never puts it in the Rashtrakuta shape.

region.text: the Rashtrakuta core, Manyakheta and the Deccan, taken by Tailapa II

ledger.note: 973: Tailapa II takes the Deccan. 'Tailapa dethroned Karka and established a new dynasty' after Siyaka's 972 sack of Manyakheta. The Western Chalukya shape of Cliopatria begins only in 980.

region.text: Indra IV's seat, wholly in Ganga country: Cliopatria's 980 shape on the Mysore plateau

ledger.note: 973: the Rashtrakuta remnant stands in Gangavadi. 'Krishna's grandson Indra, supported by the Ganga chief Marasimha, disputed Tailapa's ascension'; Marasimha was 'a powerful Rashtrakuta feudatory from the Ganga family' (Tailapa II page). The page places Indra IV's resistance nowhere; the only ground is Cliopatria's 980 shape (22,508 km2), which lies wholly in the Mysore region and nowhere in its Western Chalukya shape. The remnant is drawn over the Ganga tint of 819-982.

982 (bridge): Rashtrakuta overlordship ends with Indra IV. 'With Indra IV's death, the main line of the Rashtrakuta dynasty came to an end' (sallekhana on 20 March 982). No page says when the Gangas ceased to be feudatories; the same bridge as western-ganga-dynasty /ledger/11. The Western Ganga page has the Gangas 'helped King Rachamalla IV suppress a civil war in 975' and Marasimha II (died 975) among Indra IV's supporters (Tailapa II page).

982: Indra IV ends his life at Shravanabelagola and the Rashtrakuta line ends. 'Indra IV performed Sallekhana at Shravanabelagola on 20 March 982 CE.' and 'With Indra IV's death, the main line of the Rashtrakuta dynasty came to an end' (Dynasty page). The land of the remnant is Cliopatria's 980 shape (22,508 km2), which lies wholly in Ganga country (Gangavadi) and nowhere in Cliopatria's Western Chalukya 980 shape; the Western Chalukyas, who had taken the core in 973, hold the rest. Counterpart changed from western-chalukya-empire to western-ganga-dynasty (Tailapa II page: Indra IV's backer was the Ganga chief Marasimha); Gangavadi is Ganga land to the Chola conquest.

wars.name: Rashtrakuta overthrow of the Badami Chalukyas
wars.outcome: Dantidurga defeated Kirtivarman II's army in 753 (Samangadh plate) and took the north; Krishna I defeated Kirtivarman II, 'the last Badami Chalukya emperor', in 757.
wars.note: The Dynasty page dates the first defeat to 753; the Krishna I page, the second to 757.

wars.name: Tripartite struggle for Kannauj
wars.outcome: Dhruva beat Vatsaraja and Dharmapala and went home in 790; Govinda III beat Nagabhata II near Gwalior and received the submission of Chakrayudha and Dharmapala (800). 'With Govinda's death in 814, the Rashtrakuta threat finally lapsed' and Nagabhata II took Kannauj in 816.
wars.note: The Rashtrakutas never held the north; the shapes of Cliopatria for 788-792 and 922-925 are corrected.

wars.name: Rashtrakuta wars with the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi
wars.outcome: Dhruva humbled Vishnuvardhana IV in 784 and made a marriage alliance (786); Amoghavarsha I's war at Vingavalli is undated; Vishnuvardhana V was killed in 846; by 850 Cliopatria's shape has lost Vengi.
wars.note: The 846 date is from the Amoghavarsha page; the Vingavalli battle and Sthambha's capture have no year there.

wars.name: Dhruva's expedition to Kanchi
wars.outcome: 'He undertook campaigns to Kanchi in 785'; the Pallava Nandivarman II was forced to accept Rashtrakuta suzerainty (undated).

wars.name: Western Ganga wars and the revolts against Amoghavarsha I
wars.outcome: Dhruva's campaign against the Western Gangas in 788; the Ganga feudatory revolt in which Shivamara II was killed in 816, further revolts 818-820 and the empire 're-established by 821'.
wars.note: The 788 campaign is from the Dhruva page.

wars.name: Indra III's northern campaign
wars.outcome: Kannauj was 'completely destroyed' and held 'until c. 916'; Mahipala I fled and the Pratiharas regained the city (undated).
wars.note: The Gurjara-Pratihara page dates the sack to about 916.

wars.name: Rashtrakuta-Chola war (Takkolam)
wars.outcome: Krishna III captured Kanchi and Tanjore (plates of 944), secured Tondaimandalam and 'in c. 949' beat the Cholas at Takkolam, killing Rajaditya (undated).
wars.note: Cliopatria's Chola shape keeps Kanchi throughout; the Chola group should settle the conflict.

wars.name: Paramara sack of Manyakheta and Tailapa's seizure
wars.outcome: In 972 the Paramara Siyaka 'invaded and sacked' Manyakheta; in 973 Tailapa II 'dethroned Karka and established a new dynasty'. Indra IV carried on until 982.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier is recorded on the pages opened; the northern raids, the Gujarat branch and the Vengi, Kanchi and Malwa feudatories are approximate throughout.

sources.title: Tailapa II
sources.note: 972 sack of Manyakheta, 973 Tailapa dethrones Karka, Indra IV d. 982.

sources.title: Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty
sources.note: Opened in the repair run: Bhoja and Gujarat ('parts of Gujarat', the Gujarat Rashtrakuta line), Govinda III (793-814), Krishna II at Ujjain c. 880, Indra III at Kannauj c. 916.

sources.title: Western Ganga dynasty
sources.note: Opened in the repair run: 'by 819, a Ganga resurgence gained them partial control over Gangavadi'; the Gangas feudatories and allies; Rashtrakuta overlordship.

sources.title: Bhauma-Kara dynasty
sources.note: Opened in the repair run: the Bhauma-Kara kingdom of Toshala (Kalinga) weakened by Rashtrakuta and Pala invasions; no kings or years for them.

notes: Rashtrakuta dynasty, Cliopatria 'Rashtrakuta Dynasty' 755-989 (17 shapes), reviewed against nine Wikipedia pages (the budget); the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty page (opened for the Pala dossier) is cited in notes only. The infobox of the Dynasty page gives no area and no capital, so no area ratio could be made; areas were checked against regions with the gazetteer instead. Cliopatria rows to correct: 788-792 and 922-925 draw the Doab raids of Dhruva (786-790) and Indra III (about 916) as territory, and the second is misdated; 806-849 includes Gujarat directly although the page makes it a cadet branch under Indra (813-888), so the ledger carries it as a vassal tint; 947-979 omits Tondaimandalam (secured by 944) and runs to 979 although Tailapa II took the core in 973; 980-989 ends seven years after Indra IV's death in 982. Conflicts: Cliopatria's Chola shapes cover Kanchi (from 898) and Tanjore (from 925) to 975, against the Krishna III page; the Dhruva (793) and Krishna I (774) pages put their deaths at Manyakheta although Amoghavarsha I is said to have built it; the Dynasty page says 'between the 6th and 10th centuries' against its own 753-982; Amoghavarsha's accession is 814 or 815 and his death 877 or 878; Cliopatria starts the Western Chalukya row in 980, the page in 973. Not dated on any page opened (recorded at confidence 1 or left out): the Gujarat branch's start (757 on the Dynasty page, 813 on the Govinda III page); Manyakheta's foundation; the Chola recovery of Tondaimandalam; Krishna II's loss of Vengi; the Paramara feudatory status (800, 914) and its end; the 880 battle at Ujjain (Gurjara-Pratihara page); Sripurusha's defeat; Pandya, Kerala and Ceylon submissions (958 plates, claims). Counterparts needing dossiers: western-ganga-dynasty (Gangavadi, Talakad; no Cliopatria row), eastern-chalukyas (Vengi), gujarat-rashtrakutas (cadet branch 757-888), Shilaharas of South Konkan, the Ayudha dynasty of Kannauj. Gazetteer names wanted: Gangavadi, Vengi, Lata (alias of Gujarat region exists), Tondaimandalam, Manyakheta (Malkhed), Achalapura (Elichpur). Wikipedia page Mahipala_I was opened by mistake (it is the Pratihara king) and not used. REPAIR RUN (2026-10-19, after the adversarial review; pages reopened: Rashtrakuta dynasty, Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty, Tailapa II; new pages: Western Ganga dynasty, Bhauma-Kara dynasty). (1) Gujarat: ledger 860 now loses the Cliopatria-dropped Gujarat to the Pratiharas (mirror of gurjara-pratihara-dynasty /ledger/20) and the Gujarat-branch tint ends at 860, not 888; the Dynasty page (757-888, Krishna II 'brought it under direct control from Manyakheta'), the Pratihara page (Krishna II at Ujjain 880; Bhoja 'exterminated the Gujarat Rashtrakuta line') and Cliopatria (Pratiharas from 860) cannot be drawn together, so 888 is kept in the note only. (2) Gangavadi: direct land to 818, a Ganga vassal tint 819-982 (mirror of western-ganga-dynasty /ledger/9-11; the Mysore region is removed from the keyframes from 819 and the 819 keyframe is new); the 973 remnant, which lies wholly in Gangavadi, is a c1 gain from the Gangas, and the 982 dissolve hands it to western-ganga-dynasty (the second successor). I disagree with the WG dossier only on the start: 757 here (Krishna I page: 'acquired territory in Gangavadi', reign 756-774) against its 780 occupation_start (Dhruva), and on the type (gain here, occupation there); the two dossiers differ by 23 years and the orchestrator or the WG author should pick one. (3) Vengi is a vassal tint only (784-850): the 772 direct gain and 850 direct loss were dropped and the Vijayawada disc was removed from the keyframes 772-849 (the Krishna I page names only Vishnuvardhana IV; the Dynasty page lists the Eastern Chalukyas among the feudatories). Kalinga, Kosala: Odisha goes to bhauma-kara-dynasty (a placeholder slug, to be listed), Chhattisgarh to nobody. (4) Contest ends aligned with the Pratihara dossier: Malwa-Gwalior 814 (Govinda III 793-814) and Kannauj 926 (Cliopatria); the Indra III page has the Rashtrakutas hold Kannauj only 'until c. 916', so 926 is a bridge adopted for consistency. Left as is (thin): the 936-947 loss of 18,462 km2 in south Gujarat, the 806 Gujarat year, Manyakheta's foundation year, the 967 loss of Tondaimandalam.
